question: If \((0.2)^x=2\) and \(\log 2=0.3010,\) then the value of \(x\) to the nearest tenth is:
solution:
Use common, base-10 logarithms. Because \(0.2=2/10\), the quotient rule gives
\[
\log(0.2)=\log2-\log10
=0.3010-1=-0.6990.
\]
Both sides of \((0.2)^x=2\) are positive, so taking logarithms is valid. The power rule brings the unknown exponent down as a multiplier:
\[
x\log(0.2)=\log2.
\]
Since \(\log(0.2)=-0.6990\ne0\), division gives
\[
x\approx\frac{0.3010}{-0.6990}
\approx-0.4306.
\]
Rounded to the nearest tenth, the value is \(-0.4\), choice C.
